doc:
Weave manoeuvring - decisive closed-cycle energy test (Sol review 595baf4, smallest test for option 3).
NON-CANON prototype lane. kT 2026-11-21: may challenge CANON II §7.1a/§7.1b; §18A doctrine waived for this lane.
ALL bodies. ALL sponsors. 2026-2226.

Rule S (canon as written): ENERGY-B arrival speed counted in the Sun-barycentric frame, Sun is the momentum partner.
Rule L (lane proposal): inside a body's sphere of influence the Weave's partner is that body; ENERGY-B is counted in its frame.
ENERGY-B (CANON II §7.1a): v_a^2 = |v_s|^2 + 2(Phi_s - Phi_a), direction carried by the local frames.
Cycle: hover at sea level -> metric up-hop 1 km -> ordinary fall 1 km with ideal harvest -> trim residual velocity -> start state.
A closed cycle must return zero net extractable work (CANON II §7.3) or it is a pump.

S (canon \u00a77.1a/b as written).verdict: PUMP: violates CANON II §7.3 (hard kill if restored)

rule_L_theorem: with Phi time-independent in the partner frame, ENERGY-B segments + ordinary gravity conserve E_mech; net work of any closed cycle = paid - harvested = losses >= 0

soi_handoff.note: IF the Weave could also rotate real velocity for free, a 180 deg turn of v_inf would be a gravity assist anywhere in the sphere of influence (planet pays): setting-scale. EXCLUDED by lane rule W-3, which keeps canon §7.1a: arrival direction is carried by the local frames and ordinary vector steering is paid by torch. The Weave changes POSITION; the torch owns VELOCITY.

rules.W1: partner = dominant body inside its sphere of influence (departs §7.1b; lane-authorized)
rules.W2: ENERGY-B counted in the partner frame; height gain paid from bank/reactor (powered channel, departs §7.1a; lane-authorized)
rules.W3: arrival kinetic state = departure state carried by local frames (canon §7.1a kept): no free velocity steering
rules.W4: doctrine §18A and near-body certification §6 waived for this lane (kT)

verdict: Rule S pumps ~0.6 GJ per 1 km cycle for 61 t (source: Sun exchange at 29.8 km/s). Rule L closes. Weave near bodies is admissible only with Rule L, which is a scoped departure from §7.1b (authorized for this lane, not canon).
